recordings.remarks: Start at 0:00 . Was recording for their locally known "flute-like" song that goes something like "D6 A6 B6 B6" ... "A6 C7 C7" that appears at the very beginning of the record at 0:00 . After that, sounds like many butcherbirds are singing many different songs on this recording. There was a whole bunch flying through the sky and perching on the very top of a huge tree. Along with other birds in the background.

recordings.location: Tom Price, Shire of Ashburton, Western Australia
recordings.remarks:
Hi,
I am hoping someone can identify this bird.
We were staying at a caravan park in Tom Price Western Australia and this bird started calling at about 5:30 at first light every morning we were there, which was 5 nights. Since it was dark I could not see the bird. It called for about an hour then stopped, and I did not hear it call at any other time period of the day.
When I first heard it I thought it was someone whistling.
It woke us both up as it was so unusual.
The recording also captures a brief call of a parrot, possibly a ringneck, so just ignore that.
recordings.carol_category: pre-dawn solo song (WA, ssp. picatus range; recordist was unsure of the ID)
